# omadafusion_switch_port (Resource)

Name and port profile of one port on an adopted switch. The port always exists, so creating this resource takes over the port and destroying it optionally resets it to `Port<N>` with the `All` profile. Per-port overrides are not managed; put VLAN and protection settings in an `omadafusion_port_profile`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Build a jack map: one entry per wall jack.
locals {
  jacks = {
    "jack-12 front desk printer" = { switch = "AA-BB-CC-00-00-02", port = 9 }
    "jack-14 exam room 2"        = { switch = "AA-BB-CC-00-00-02", port = 10 }
  }
}

resource "omadafusion_switch_port" "jack" {
  for_each   = local.jacks
  switch_mac = each.value.switch
  port       = each.value.port
  name       = each.key
  profile_id = omadafusion_port_profile.devices_access.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `port` (Number) Port number.
- `profile_id` (String) Port profile ID.
- `switch_mac` (String) Switch MAC, any common format.

### Optional

- `name` (String) Port name. Defaults to `Port<N>`.
- `reset_on_destroy` (Boolean) On destroy, rename the port to `Port<N>` and assign the `All` profile.
- `site` (String) Site name or ID. Defaults to the provider `site`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<switch_mac>/<port>`.
- `profile_name` (String) Name of the assigned profile.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <switch_mac>/<port> or <site>/<switch_mac>/<port>
terraform import omadafusion_switch_port.uplink Default/AA-BB-CC-00-00-02/24
```
